# Description

This code includes code used to analyze and visualize multiregional placenta gene expression profiling. 

# Load packages

Install the necessary packages for analysis.  

```{r Packages, warning=FALSE}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(fgsea)
library(reshape2)
library(msigdbr)
library(stringr)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidygraph)
library(pheatmap)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)
library(UpSetR)
library(corrplot)
library(BiocParallel)
library(e1071) 

```

# Read differential expression results

``` {r diff_expr_results, tidy=TRUE, tidy.opts=list(width.cutoff=60)}
# you will need to change this to the directory you are working in

output_directory = "C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Manuscripts/Placenta_gene_expression/analysis/"

hyp_femalemale_data = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,"dream_diffexpr_hyp_femalemale_batchcorr.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
```

# Scatter plots to compare differential expression by sex and hypertension

Figure 1: Compares differential expression between placentas from normotensive and hypertensive pregnancies in normotensive pregnancies in female-bearing pregnancies (x-axis) versus male-bearing pregnancies (y-axis).

Figure 2: Compares differential expression between male and female placentas in normotensive pregnancies (x-axis) versus hypertensive pregnancies (y-axis).

```{r diff_expr_scatter}

# ------- hyp:norm diff in male vs female -------

merged_data = merge(male_normhyp_data, female_normhyp_data, by = "genes")
merged_data = merged_data %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "both_sig",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "both_nom_sig",
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y >= 0.05 ~ "sig_male",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y >= 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_male",
      adj.P.Val.x >= 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "sig_female",
      P.Value.x >= 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_female",
      TRUE       ~ "not"
    )
  )
merged_data_label = merged_data %>%
  group_by(sig) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = abs(logFC.x), n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = logFC.x, y = logFC.y, color = sig, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_point() +
  #scale_color_manual(values = c("both_sig" = "red", "sig_male" = "blue","sig_female" = "orange", "not" = "grey")) +
  #scale_alpha_manual(values = c("both_sig" = 0.9, "sig_male" = 0.9,"sig_female" = 0.9, "not" = 0.3)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("both_sig" = "red", "both_nom_sig" = "pink", "sig_male" = "blue", "nom_sig_male" = "lightblue", "sig_female" = "orange", "nom_sig_female" = "khaki1", "not" = "grey")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("both_sig" = 0.9, "both_nom_sig" = 0.7, "sig_male" = 0.9, "nom_sig_male" = 0.7, "sig_female" = 0.9, "nom_sig_female" = 0.7, "not" = 0.3)) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = merged_data_label,
    aes(label = genes),
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave(paste0(output_directory, "scatter_malehyp_femalehyp.pdf"))


# ------- sex diff in norm vs hyp -------

merged_data = merge(norm_femalemale_data, hyp_femalemale_data, by = "genes")
merged_data = merged_data %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "both_sig",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "both_nom_sig",
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y >= 0.05 ~ "sig_norm",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y >= 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_norm",
      adj.P.Val.x >= 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "sig_hyp",
      P.Value.x >= 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_hyp",
      TRUE       ~ "not"
    )
  )

merged_data_label = merged_data %>%
  group_by(sig) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = abs(logFC.x), n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = logFC.x, y = logFC.y, color = sig, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_point() +
  #xlim(-5,5) +
  #ylim(-5,5)  +
  #scale_color_manual(values = c("both_sig" = "red", "sig_norm" = "green","sig_hyp" = "purple", "not" = "grey")) +
  #scale_alpha_manual(values = c("both_sig" = 0.9, "sig_norm" = 0.9,"sig_hyp" = 0.9, "not" = 0.3)) +
```

# Visualization of differentially expressed genes

This creates box plots that show the expression of specific genes in each of the 4 placenta sample groups: male placentas from normotensive pregnancies, female placentas from normotensive pregnancies, male placentas from hypertensive pregnancies, and female placentas from hypertensive pregnancies.

Genes visualized were chosen based on significant differnetial expression, which in this case is defined as adjusted p-value < 0.05 using limma-voom for differential expression after accounting for multiregional sampling.

The first plot shows autosomal genes that showed significant differential expression between male and female placentas in normotensive pregnancies, hypertensive pregnancies, or both. 

The second plot shows genes that showed genes differentially expressed between placentas from normotensive versus hypertensive pregnancies, in females, males, or both.

```{r sig_gene_boxplots}

```

# Gene Set Enrichment Analysis 

```{r gsea}

# list of differential expression profiles to analyze
datasets = list("norm_femalemale" = data.frame(norm_femalemale_data), "hyp_femalemale" = data.frame(hyp_femalemale_data), "male_normhyp" = data.frame(male_normhyp_data), "female_normhyp" = data.frame(female_normhyp_data))

sig_pathways_list = list()

for (name in names(datasets)) {

  print (name)
  
  dataset = datasets[[name]]
  
  # Create ranked vector
  # Ranking measure used: moderated t-statistic
  ranks = dataset$t
  
  # Names must be gene symbols (or whatever ID matches pathway genes)
  names(ranks) = dataset$genes
  
  # Remove duplicates and NAs
  ranks = ranks[!is.na(ranks)]
  ranks = sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)
  
  # Get Hallmark pathways from MSigDB
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",collection = "H")
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
  msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY")
  
  pathways = split(msig$gene_symbol, msig$gs_name)
  
  # Run fgsea
  suppressWarnings({
    fgseaRes = fgsea(
      pathways = pathways,
      stats = ranks,
      minSize = 15,
      maxSize = 500,
      BPPARAM = SerialParam()
    )
  })
  
  # Sort by significance
  fgseaRes = fgseaRes[order(fgseaRes$padj), ]
  
  # write out results
  fgseaRes_out = as.data.frame(fgseaRes)
  fgseaRes_out$leadingEdge = sapply(fgseaRes_out$leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ",")
  #write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(output_directory,"t_fgsea_H_results_", name, ".csv"))
  #write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(output_directory,"t_fgsea_GOBP_results_", name, ".csv"))
  write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(output_directory,"t_fgsea_KEGG_results_", name, ".csv"))
  
  padj_threshold = 0.01 # 0.01 for H and KEGG, 0.001 for GO BP
  
  # save sig pathways
  sig_pathways_list[[name]] = fgseaRes$pathway[fgseaRes$padj < padj_threshold]
  
  # plot bubble plot
  plot_df = as.data.frame(fgseaRes) %>%
  filter(padj < padj_threshold)

  bubble_plot = ggplot(plot_df,
         aes(x = NES,
             y = reorder(pathway, NES),
             size = size,
             color = -log10(padj))) +
    geom_point() +
    ggtitle(name) +
    theme_bw()
  print(bubble_plot)
  #ggsave(plot = bubble_plot, filename = paste0(output_directory,"t_fgsea_H_bubbleplot_", name, ".pdf"), height = 8, width = 8)
  #ggsave(plot = bubble_plot, filename = paste0(output_directory,"t_fgsea_GOBP_bubbleplot_", name, ".pdf"), height = 12, width = 16)
  ggsave(plot = bubble_plot, filename = paste0(output_directory,"t_fgsea_KEGG_bubbleplot_", name, ".pdf"), height = 8, width = 8)

}


```

# Compare gene set enrichment across sexes

Here we will calculate gene set enrichment using several gene set collections for genes ranked on difference between hypertensive pregnancy placentas and normotensive pregnancy placentas for males vs females.  

```{r compare_gsea}

# Get gene sets from MSigDB

msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",collection = "H")
tag = "H"

# msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
# tag = "GOBP"

# msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY")
# tag = "KEGG"

pathways = split(msig$gene_symbol, msig$gs_name)

# data sets to compare
male_hypnorm_dataset = data.frame(male_normhyp_data)
female_hypnorm_dataset = data.frame(female_normhyp_data)

# ------- male normhyp ---------

# Create ranked vector
# Common choice: moderated t-statistic
male_hypnorm_ranks = male_hypnorm_dataset$t

# Names must be gene symbols (or whatever ID matches pathway genes)
names(male_hypnorm_ranks) = male_hypnorm_dataset$genes

# Remove duplicates and NAs
male_hypnorm_ranks = male_hypnorm_ranks[!is.na(male_hypnorm_ranks)]
male_hypnorm_ranks = sort(male_hypnorm_ranks, decreasing = TRUE)

# Run fgsea
suppressWarnings({
  fgseaRes_male_hypnorm = fgsea(
    pathways = pathways,
    stats = male_hypnorm_ranks,
    minSize = 15,
    maxSize = 500,
    BPPARAM = SerialParam()
  )
})

# Sort by significance
fgseaRes_male_hypnorm = fgseaRes_male_hypnorm[order(fgseaRes_male_hypnorm$padj), ]

# ------- female normhyp ---------

# Create ranked vector
# Common choice: moderated t-statistic
female_hypnorm_ranks = female_hypnorm_dataset$t

# Names must be gene symbols (or whatever ID matches pathway genes)
names(female_hypnorm_ranks) = female_hypnorm_dataset$genes

# Remove duplicates and NAs
female_hypnorm_ranks = female_hypnorm_ranks[!is.na(female_hypnorm_ranks)]
female_hypnorm_ranks = sort(female_hypnorm_ranks, decreasing = TRUE)

# Run fgsea
suppressWarnings({
  fgseaRes_female_hypnorm = fgsea(
    pathways = pathways,
    stats = female_hypnorm_ranks,
    minSize = 15,
    maxSize = 500,
    BPPARAM = SerialParam()
  )
})

# Sort by significance
fgseaRes_female_hypnorm = fgseaRes_female_hypnorm[order(fgseaRes_female_hypnorm$padj), ]

# compare results

comp = merge(
  fgseaRes_male_hypnorm[, c("pathway", "NES", "padj")],
  fgseaRes_female_hypnorm[, c("pathway", "NES", "padj")],
  by = "pathway",
  suffixes = c("_male", "_fem")
)
write.csv(comp, file = paste0(output_directory, "compare_fgsea_",tag,"_male_female_hypnorm.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# focus on gene sets significant in males or females
sig_comp = subset(comp, padj_male < 0.05 | padj_fem < 0.05)
sig_comp_color = ifelse(sig_comp$padj_male < 0.05 & sig_comp$padj_fem < 0.05,"red",ifelse(sig_comp$padj_male < 0.05, "blue", ifelse(sig_comp$padj_fem < 0.05, "orange", "grey70")))

# plot comparison
ggplot(comp, aes(x = NES_male, y = NES_fem)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey70") +
  geom_point(data = sig_comp, color = sig_comp_color) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = sig_comp,
    aes(label = pathway),
    size = 2,
    max.overlaps = 30
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "NES, male, hyp vs norm", y = "NES, female, hyp vs norm")
ggsave(filename = paste0(output_directory, "compare_",tag,"_male_female_hypnorm.pdf"), height = 6, width = 10)

```


# Intraplacental variance

This block calculates intraplacental variance as the residual variance in gene expression after fitting a trend to the mean expression level.

After calculating, gene set enrichment analysis on genes sorted by intraplacental variation is used to see what is enriched in highly and lowly varying genes.

```{r intraplac_var}

# load gene expression data
lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/lcpm_norm_batchcorrected.csv")
rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data) = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data$gene
lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data$gene = NULL

pheno = data.frame(colnames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)[-1])
colnames(pheno) = c("sample")
pheno$sex = ifelse(grepl("XY",pheno$sample, fixed = TRUE),"male","female")
pheno$status = ifelse(grepl("Cont",pheno$sample, fixed = TRUE),"normotensive","hypertensive")
pheno$placenta = str_split(pheno$sample, "_", simplify = TRUE)[, 1]
pheno$quadrant = str_split(pheno$sample, "_", simplify = TRUE)[, 2]
pheno$sex_status = paste0(pheno$sex, "_", pheno$status)

# create placenta level pheno file for merging later
pheno_placenta = pheno
pheno_placenta$sample = NULL
pheno_placenta$quadrant = NULL
pheno_placenta = pheno_placenta[!duplicated(pheno_placenta$placenta), ]

# Ensure pheno matches expression matrix
lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data[,pheno$sample]
stopifnot(all(pheno$sample == colnames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)))

placentas = unique(pheno$placenta)

residual_var_list = list()

for(placenta in placentas){

    placenta_samples = pheno$sample[
        pheno$placenta == placenta
    ]

    expr_placenta = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data[, placenta_samples, drop = FALSE]

    # Mean expression per gene
    gene_mean = rowMeans(expr_placenta)

    # Variance across individuals
    gene_var = apply(expr_placenta, 1, var)

    # Avoid log(0)
    gene_var[gene_var <= 0] = min(
        gene_var[gene_var > 0]
    ) / 2

    # Fit mean-variance trend
    fit = loess(
        log10(gene_var) ~ gene_mean,
        span = 0.5
    )

    # Residual variability
    resid_var = residuals(fit)

    residual_var_list[[placenta]] = data.frame(
        gene = rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data),
        mean_logCPM = gene_mean,
        variance = gene_var,
        residual_variability = resid_var
    )
}

residual_var_mat = do.call(
    cbind,
    lapply(
        residual_var_list,
        function(x) x$residual_variability
    )
)

rownames(residual_var_mat) = rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)

# grab high variance genes 
high_var_genes = lapply(
  residual_var_list,
  function(df) {
    df$gene[df$residual_variability > 1]
  }
)

# tally genes identified as variable

# Combine all genes from all tissues
all_genes = unlist(high_var_genes)

# Count occurrences
gene_counts = table(all_genes)

# Convert to data frame
gene_count_df = data.frame(
  gene = names(gene_counts),
  n_tissues = as.integer(gene_counts),
  row.names = NULL
)

# Sort by number of tissues
gene_count_df = gene_count_df[
  order(gene_count_df$n_tissues, decreasing = TRUE),
]

# plot genes with high residual variation and high expression

# merge with precalculated average expression values
var_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/variance_with_means.csv")
var_data$AveExp = rowMeans(var_data[,grepl("AveExpr_",colnames(var_data))])
gene_count_df$AveExpr = var_data$AveExp[match(gene_count_df$gene,var_data$Geneid)]
gene_count_df_filter = gene_count_df[gene_count_df$AveExpr > 1,]

genes_to_plot = gene_count_df_filter$gene[gene_count_df_filter$n_tissues == 20]
genes_to_plot = genes_to_plot[1:5]

# filter for genes of interest
expr_data_for_plotting = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data
expr_data_for_plotting$gene = rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)

for (selected_gene in genes_to_plot) {
  if (! selected_gene %in% expr_data_for_plotting$gene) {  print (paste(selected_gene, "not in dataset"))}
  
  gene_expr = expr_data_for_plotting[expr_data_for_plotting$gene == selected_gene,]
  gene_expr_long = melt(gene_expr)
  colnames(gene_expr_long) = c("gene","sample","expression")
  gene_expr_long = merge(gene_expr_long, pheno, by = "sample")
  
  # plot gene expression in 4 groups
  gene_expr_long$sex_status = factor(gene_expr_long$sex_status, levels = c("male_normotensive", "male_hypertensive", "female_normotensive","female_hypertensive"))
  gene_expr_long$placenta = factor(gene_expr_long$placenta, levels = unique(pheno$placenta))
  gene_expr_long$sample = factor(gene_expr_long$sample, levels = pheno$sample)
  
  plot = ggplot(gene_expr_long, aes(x = placenta, y = expression, color = sex_status, group = sex_status, fill = sex_status)) + 
    geom_jitter(alpha  = 0.75, width = 0.2) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha  = 0.75) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("lightblue", "blue","gold", "orange")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("lightblue", "blue","gold", "orange")) +
    ggtitle(selected_gene) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 90, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)) 
  print(plot)
}

# enrichment analysis in genes that have high variance in all placentas
variable_all_tissues = gene_count_df$gene[gene_count_df$n_tissues == 20 & gene_count_df$AveExpr > 1]
all_convert = mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db,
                  keys = variable_all_tissues,
                  keytype = "SYMBOL",
                  column = "ENTREZID",
                  multiVals = "first")

all = na.omit(unname(all_convert)) 
 
bp = enrichGO(
  gene          = all,
  OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType       = "ENTREZID",
  ont           = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff  = 0.1,
  readable      = TRUE
)
mf = enrichGO(
  gene          = all,
  OrgDb         = org.Hs.eg.db,
  keyType       = "ENTREZID",
  ont           = "MF",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH",
  pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
  qvalueCutoff  = 0.1,
  readable      = TRUE
)

dotplot(bp, showCategory = 30) + ggtitle("High residual variance - GO BP enrichment") + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))
dotplot(mf, showCategory = 30) + ggtitle("High residual variance - GO MF enrichment") + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6))

bp_readable = setReadable(bp, 'org.Hs.eg.db', 'ENTREZID')
cnetplot(bp_readable)

# mean by var

plot(
    gene_mean,
    log10(gene_var),
    pch = 16,
    cex = 0.4
)

ord <- order(gene_mean)

lines(
    gene_mean[ord],
    predict(fit)[ord],
    col = "red",
    lwd = 2
)

# correlation across placentas

cor_mat = cor(residual_var_mat,
               method = "pearson",
               use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

corrplot(
  cor_mat,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  order = "hclust",
  addCoef.col = "black",
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.srt = 45,
  number.cex = 0.3,
  diag = FALSE,
  col = colorRampPalette(
    c("blue", "white", "red")
  )(200)
) 

# get percent ranks

percent_rank_mat = apply(
  residual_var_mat,
  2,
  function(x) rank(x, ties.method = "average") / length(x)
)

percent_rank_mat = as.matrix(percent_rank_mat)

rownames(percent_rank_mat) = rownames(residual_var_mat)

write.csv(as.data.frame(residual_var_mat), file = paste0(output_directory, "residual_var.csv"))
write.csv(as.data.frame(percent_rank_mat), file = paste0(output_directory, "residual_var_percentrank.csv"))

# gsea for genes ranked by median residual variance across all placentas
res_var_medians = rowMedians(residual_var_mat)
names(res_var_medians) = rownames(residual_var_mat)
res_var_medians = sort(res_var_medians, decreasing = TRUE)

# histogram of median variance
res_var_medians_df = as.data.frame(res_var_medians)
res_var_median_stats = res_var_medians_df %>%
  summarise(
    mean_val = mean(res_var_medians),
    median_val = median(res_var_medians),
    skew_val = skewness(res_var_medians)
  )

ggplot(res_var_medians_df, aes(x = res_var_medians)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  geom_vline(data = res_var_median_stats, aes(xintercept = mean_val), 
             color = "red", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("label", x = max(res_var_medians_df$res_var_medians) * 0.6, y = 1000,
           label = paste(
             "Mean:", round(res_var_median_stats$mean_val, 2), "\n",
             "Median:", round(res_var_median_stats$median_val, 2), "\n",
             "Skew:", round(res_var_median_stats$skew_val, 2)
           ),
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, color = "black",
           size = 4, fontface = "bold",
           fill = "white") +
  theme_minimal()
print(res_var_median_stats)
ggsave(filename = paste0(output_directory, "residual_var_medians_histogram.pdf"))

# Get Hallmark pathways from MSigDB
msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",collection = "H")
#msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
#msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY")

pathways = split(msig$gene_symbol, msig$gs_name)

# Run fgsea
suppressWarnings({
  fgseaRes = fgsea(
    pathways = pathways,
    stats = res_var_medians,
    minSize = 15,
    maxSize = 500
  )
})

# Sort by significance
fgseaRes = fgseaRes[order(fgseaRes$padj), ]

# write out results
fgseaRes_out = as.data.frame(fgseaRes)
fgseaRes_out$leadingEdge = sapply(fgseaRes_out$leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ",")
write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(output_directory, "median_res_var_H_fgsea.csv"))

# plot gsea results by residual variance

plot_df = as.data.frame(fgseaRes) %>%
  filter(padj < 0.01) # 0.01 for H, 0.001 for GO BP
  
bubble_plot = ggplot(plot_df,
       aes(x = NES,
           y = reorder(pathway, NES),
           # size = size,
           # color = -log10(padj))) +
           size = -log10(padj),
           color = NES)) +
  geom_point() + 
  scale_color_gradient2(low = "royalblue3", mid = "white", high = "firebrick3",midpoint = median(res_var_medians_df$res_var_medians, na.rm = TRUE)) +
  ggtitle("Ranked by Median Residual Variance") +
  theme_bw()
print(bubble_plot)
ggsave(plot = bubble_plot, filename = paste0(output_directory,"fgsea_H_bubbleplot_residual_var.pdf"), height = 6, width = 9)


#----------------
# plot top residual variance genes
top_res_var_genes = names(res_var_medians[1:5])

expr_data_for_plotting = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data
expr_data_for_plotting$gene = rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)

for (selected_gene in top_res_var_genes) {
  if (! selected_gene %in% expr_data_for_plotting$gene) {  print (paste(selected_gene, "not in dataset"))}
  
  gene_expr = expr_data_for_plotting[expr_data_for_plotting$gene == selected_gene,]
  gene_expr_long = melt(gene_expr)
  colnames(gene_expr_long) = c("gene","sample","expression")
  gene_expr_long = merge(gene_expr_long, pheno, by = "sample")
  
  # plot gene expression in 4 groups
  gene_expr_long$sex_status = factor(gene_expr_long$sex_status, levels = c("male_normotensive", "male_hypertensive", "female_normotensive","female_hypertensive"))
  gene_expr_long$placenta = factor(gene_expr_long$placenta, levels = unique(pheno$placenta))
  gene_expr_long$sample = factor(gene_expr_long$sample, levels = pheno$sample)
  
  plot = ggplot(gene_expr_long, aes(x = placenta, y = expression, color = sex_status, group = sex_status, fill = sex_status)) + 
    geom_jitter(alpha  = 0.75, width = 0.2) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha  = 0.75) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("lightblue", "blue","gold", "orange")) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("lightblue", "blue","gold", "orange")) +
    ggtitle(selected_gene) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 90, vjust = 1, hjust = 1)) 
  print(plot)
}
```

# Differential expression of placenta preeclampsia marker genes
```{r PE_diffexp}

PE_marker_table = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/repeat_profile/placenta_PE_markers_all_datasets.csv", check.names = FALSE, header = TRUE)

# filter for pval columns

pv_columns = PE_marker_table[, grepl("_pval", colnames(PE_marker_table), fixed = TRUE)]
rownames(pv_columns) = PE_marker_table$`Gene symbol`
pv_columns = na.omit(pv_columns)

# convert data for easier plots

row_order <- rownames(pv_columns)
col_order <- colnames(pv_columns)

heat_df = pv_columns %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(-Gene,
               names_to = "Profile",
               values_to = "pvalue") %>%
  mutate(
    Gene = factor(Gene, levels = rev(row_order)),
    Profile = factor(Profile, levels = col_order)
  )

# plot heatmap 

ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = Profile, y = Gene, fill = pvalue)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "red",
    high = "white",
    na.value = "grey70"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1))

# try discrete values

heat_df$Profile = factor(heat_df$Profile, levels = c(
  "Horii_male_normhyp_pval",
  "VW_male_normhyp_pval",
  "Smith_male_normhyp_pval",
  "Horii_fem_normhyp_pval",
  "VW_fem_normhyp_pval",
  "Smith_fem_normhyp_pval"))
heat_df = heat_df %>%
  mutate(
    sig_category = case_when(
      is.na(pvalue)      ~ "NA",
      pvalue < 0.05      ~ "<0.05",
      pvalue < 0.10      ~ "0.05-0.10",
      TRUE               ~ ">=0.10"
    )
  )

ggplot(heat_df, aes(x = Profile, y = Gene, fill = sig_category)) +
  geom_tile(color = "lightgrey", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "<0.05"     = "maroon",
      "0.05-0.10" = "pink",
      ">=0.10"    = "white",
      "NA"        = "grey70"
    ),
    name = "P-value"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
ggsave(paste0(output_directory,"placenta_PE_markers_all_datasets_heatmap.pdf"), height = 6, width = 5)

# bar chart version

sig_counts = heat_df %>%
  group_by(Profile) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sig = sum(pvalue < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

sig_counts = sig_counts %>%
  mutate(
    Dataset = case_when(
      grepl("VW_",Profile)      ~ "Valleywise",
      grepl("Horii",Profile)      ~ "Horii",
      grepl("Smith",Profile)      ~ "Smith",
    )
  )

VW_data = sig_counts[sig_counts$Dataset == "Valleywise",]
Horii_data = sig_counts[sig_counts$Dataset == "Horii",]
Smith_data = sig_counts[sig_counts$Dataset == "Smith",]

ggplot(VW_data, aes(x = Profile, y = n_sig)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    x = "Comparison",
    y = "Genes with p < 0.05"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) 

ggplot(Horii_data, aes(x = Profile, y = n_sig)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    x = "Comparison",
    y = "Genes with p < 0.05"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) 

ggplot(Smith_data, aes(x = Profile, y = n_sig)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    x = "Comparison",
    y = "Genes with p < 0.05"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  ) 

# count pv < 0.05 and abs(logFC) > 1

df = PE_marker_table[, ! colnames(PE_marker_table) %in% c("Gene symbol","Gene name","Chromosomal location","Encodes extracellular protein","1st trimester expression","Expression in pre-eclampsia","References")]
rownames(df) = PE_marker_table$`Gene symbol`

profiles = names(df) |>
  sub("_(pval|adjpval|logFC)$", "", x = _) |>
  unique()

sig_counts = lapply(profiles, function (prof) {
  pcol <- paste0( prof, "_pval")
  fcol <- paste0( prof, "_logFC")

  n_sig <- sum(df[[pcol]] < 0.05 & abs(df[[fcol]]) > 1, na.rm = TRUE)

  data.frame(
    profile = prof,
    n_sig = n_sig
  )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

sig_counts$profile = factor(sig_counts$profile, levels = sig_counts$profile)

sig_counts = sig_counts %>%
```

# Heatmap that shows which hallmark gene sets include placenta PE marker genes

```{r PE_marker_hallmarks}

annotation_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/placenta_PE_markers_metascape_annotation.csv", check.names = FALSE)

median_res_var_gsea_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/median_res_var_H_fgsea.csv", check.names = FALSE)
median_res_var_gsea_data = median_res_var_gsea_data[order(median_res_var_gsea_data$NES, decreasing = TRUE),]
sig_gene_sets = median_res_var_gsea_data[median_res_var_gsea_data$padj<0.01,]

placenta_PE_marker_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/repeat_profile/placenta_PE_markers_all_datasets.csv", check.names = FALSE)
placenta_PE_marker_data = na.omit(placenta_PE_marker_data)

# get all the Hallmark gene sets that were significant in the variance GSEA results
sig_var_gene_sets = median_res_var_gsea_data$pathway[median_res_var_gsea_data$padj < 0.01]

# make a data frame with the sig gene sets as columns and PE genes as rows
sig_df = data.frame(matrix(ncol = length(sig_var_gene_sets), nrow = nrow(placenta_PE_marker_data)))
colnames(sig_df) = sig_var_gene_sets
rownames(sig_df) = placenta_PE_marker_data$`Gene symbol`

# fill data frame by asking if the gene is in the Hallmark data set by Metascape
for (gene in rownames(sig_df)) {
  pathways = annotation_data$`Hallmark Gene Sets`[annotation_data$`Gene Symbol` == gene]

  pathways = strsplit(pathways, "; ")[[1]]
  pathways = trimws(pathways)
  pathways = sub("^\\([^)]*\\)", "", pathways)
  pathways = gsub(" ","_",pathways)

  for (gene_set in colnames(sig_df)) {
    sig_df[gene, gene_set] = as.integer(gene_set %in% pathways)
  }
}

# make a heatmap
heatmap_df = sig_df %>%
  rownames_to_column("Gene") %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Gene,
    names_to = "Gene_Set",
    values_to = "Present"
  )

heatmap_df$Gene = factor(heatmap_df$Gene, levels = rev(placenta_PE_marker_data$`Gene symbol`))
heatmap_df$Gene_Set = factor(heatmap_df$Gene_Set, levels = sig_gene_sets$pathway)
ggplot(heatmap_df, aes(x = Gene_Set, y = Gene, fill = factor(Present))) +
  geom_tile(color = "grey70",linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("0" = "white", "1" = "darkred"),
    name = "Present"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 90,
      hjust = 0
    ),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Hallmark Gene Set",
    y = "Marker Gene"
  )
ggsave(paste0(output_directory,"placenta_PE_markers_hallmark_heatmap.pdf"), height = 8, width = 6)
```

# Network graph representation of significantly enriched gene sets

```{r gsea_graph}

# load gsea results
gsea_file = "t_fgsea_all3_results_female_normhyp_filter_padj_fract06_DEGfilter.csv"
DEG_file = "dream_diffexpr_female_hypnorm_batchcorr.csv"
direction = "both"
  
input_directory = "C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/"

# load gsea results
df = read.csv(paste0(input_directory, gsea_file), check.names = FALSE)

# load differential gene expression results
DEG_data = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,DEG_file), check.names = FALSE)
colnames(DEG_data)[colnames(DEG_data) == "genes"] = "gene"
DEG_data$t = DEG_data$t * -1 # t reversed

if (direction == "up") {
  df = df[df$NES > 0,]
} else if (direction == "down") {
  df = df[df$NES < 0,]
} else if (direction == "both") {
  # do nothing, no filtering
}

gene_counts = df %>%
  filter(!is.na(leadingEdge), leadingEdge != "") %>%
  separate_rows(leadingEdge, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(gene = str_trim(leadingEdge)) %>%
  filter(gene != "") %>%
  count(gene, sort = TRUE)

plot_df = merge(gene_counts, DEG_data, by = "gene")

fgseaRes = df %>%
  mutate(leadingEdge = strsplit(leadingEdge, ","))

edges = fgseaRes %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES, padj, leadingEdge) %>%
  unnest_longer(leadingEdge, values_to = "gene") %>%
  mutate(gene = str_trim(gene)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gene), gene != "") %>%
  distinct(pathway, gene)

pathway_nodes = fgseaRes %>%
  transmute(
    name = pathway,
    type = "pathway",
    NES = NES,
    padj = padj,
    plot_size = -log10(padj + 1e-300)   # larger = more significant
  ) %>%
  distinct(name, .keep_all = TRUE)

gene_nodes = edges %>%
  count(gene, name = "degree") %>%
  transmute(
    name = gene,
    type = "gene",
    NES = NA_real_,
    padj = NA_real_,
    plot_size = 2 
  )

gene_nodes = gene_nodes %>%
    left_join(
        DEG_data %>%
            dplyr::select(gene, t),
        by = c("name" = "gene")
    ) %>%
    mutate(plot_size = 2)

nodes = bind_rows(pathway_nodes, gene_nodes)

g = graph_from_data_frame(
  d = edges %>% dplyr::select(from = pathway, to = gene),
  directed = FALSE,
  vertices = nodes
)

set.seed(123)

ggraph(g, layout = "stress") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.15, color = "grey70") +
  geom_node_point(
    data = function(x) dplyr::filter(x, type == "pathway"),
    aes(size = -log10(padj)),
    fill = ifelse(grepl("female",gsea_file,fixed = TRUE), "orange", "darkblue"),
    shape = 21
  ) +
  geom_node_point(
    data = function(x) dplyr::filter(x, type == "gene"),
    aes(size = plot_size,
        fill = t),
    shape = 21,
    colour = "black",
    stroke = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    data = function(x) dplyr::filter(x, type == "pathway"),
    aes(label = name),
    repel = TRUE,
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  geom_node_text(
    data = function(x) dplyr::filter(x, type == "gene"),
    aes(label = name),
    repel = TRUE,
    size = 2,
    color = "grey20"
  ) +
  #scale_fill_manual(values = c(pathway = "steelblue", gene = "tomato")) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "royalblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 0
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 10)) +
  theme_void() +
  labs(fill = NULL, size = NULL)

outputfile = paste0(output_directory, gsub(".csv",paste0("_network_", direction, ".pdf"), gsea_file))
ggsave(outputfile, width = 10, height = 10)

```
